subject: Re: Load test & sizing ask — committed GPU pool / pricing bands
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@datawave.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+bench@datawave.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing — initial load test attached

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran a quick internal ramp against our current prototype and attaching the CSV with request rates and error counts. Short summary:
- Peak sustained linearized TPS seen: ~680 TPS for short bursts (30s) across our 4-node client fleet
- Stable 95th latency with our current model (13B quantized) is ~310ms at ~250 TPS; above 400 TPS we see p95 jump and some tail errors
- KV cache hit rate for repeated prefixes is ~47% in our traces

We need a committed plan that guarantees 250 TPS sustained for business hours with options to burst to 600 TPS for short windows. We're evaluating dedicated pools (monthly commit) vs hosted credits. Pricing is the sticking point — we'd like to understand discount bands if we commit to 24/7 reserved capacity vs seasonal reserved.

Can you confirm what measurements you need from our side and whether Redwood can provide an independent run (your infra) to validate sizing for the 250 TPS SLO? Also include what the SLA looks like for throughput and latency.

Thanks — Tara
Tara Singh
CTO, DataWave

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Tara Singh <tara@datawave.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing — initial load test attached

Tara,

Appreciate the CSV — that's exactly the kind of signal we need. Yes, we can run an independent validation on Redwood Dedicated and share TPS/latency traces and slot utilization. High level replies:
- Committed tier we typically size by sustained TPS target + 20% headroom (so for 250 TPS SLO we'd start with a pool sized to >300 TPS sustained).
- Bursting to 600 TPS for short windows is possible via configured burst capacity; we map burst to either warm spare slots or short-term autoscale. Bursts above committed capacity have different SLAs and are best covered by negotiated burst buckets.
- For pricing: discount bands are a function of monthly committed GPU-hours and term (12/24/36 months). We provide steeper discounts for absolute reserved spend and for multi-region redundancy.

Next steps I propose:
1) We run a Redwood-hosted benchmark using your payload and the 13B quantized variant you used. Please confirm any auth/tokens we need to replay calls.
2) Dylan will run a 6-hour sustained and a 10-minute burst test and attach traces.
3) We'll return a sizing recommendation and a pricing ladder: commit levels -> effective $/hour -> discount percent -> burst allowances.

I'll kick this off after you confirm the replay details.

- Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Tara / Olga —

We completed two passes on Redwood Dedicated using your payload and the quantized 13B model. Attachments: redwood_dedicated_eval_report_20260920.pdf and traces_p95_p99_20260921.json (subset). Short findings:
- 250 TPS sustained target: requires 3 x A100-80GB-equivalent serving slots when we run with our continuous-batching config and prefix caching enabled. Observed sustained p95 latency: 270ms; p99: 1.9s during cold-start windows.
- 10-minute burst to target 600 TPS: achieveable with autoscale + 2 warm spare slots (total 5 slots). Observed p95 during burst: ~420ms; tail increased only when KV cache miss ratio rose above ~60%.
- Cost implication: estimated committed monthly GPU-hours for the recommended pool (3 slots 24/7) = ~5,184 GPU-hours/month. We mapped price bands: 6-month commit -> 12% discount; 12-month -> 18%; 24-month -> 25% (these are illustrative pending final procurement).
- Failure modes: sustained burst over 15m without cache priming increases tail latency and memory pressure — we recommend a canary ramp policy and an explicit cache-warm step before business-critical bursts.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our infra/finance teams:
- The 5,184 GPU-hours estimate maps to an annual committed spend that we need to square with our procurement policy. Can you translate the estimate into an effective $/1M tokens and into a monthly committed fee (before discount)?
- Regarding the burst: we'd prefer the burst allowance baked into the commit (e.g., commit to baseline + 200 TPS burst included up to X hours/month) rather than relying on ad-hoc autoscale. Can you put an example pricing ladder that ties burst hours to discount?
- On SLAs: we need a clear definition for throughput SLO (e.g., 250 TPS with p95 <= 300ms 99% of the time) and credits if not met. Is that something Redwood will commit to for a reserved pool?

Also attaching our sample traces (datawave_initial_loadtest.csv) — the spikes are from our client-side backoff that we can smooth.

— Tara

Tara —

Routing answers and a concrete example below. I've attached the pricing ladder as an excerpt in the PDF we shared earlier but I pulled the key lines here so you don't need to dig through the full doc: 

Example (baseline, pre-discount):
- 3-slot pool (A100-80GB-equivalent) sized for 250 TPS sustained -> estimated pre-discount fee: $73,000/month (this includes 24/7 GPU-hours, software, and basic logging retention).
- Burst allowance option A: include up to 1200 burst-minutes/month (equiv to 20 burst-hours) that allow short windows to reach 600 TPS. If purchased as part of a 12-month commit, price = baseline * 0.82 (18% off) + burst bucket at $1,200 per 100 burst-minutes.
- Burst option B (more generous): 6000 burst-minutes/month included if you sign a 24-month commit at 25% off baseline.

SLA / throughput guarantees: we can commit to the SLO you proposed (250 TPS with p95 <= 300ms) for the baseline pool provided: (a) the workload uses the validated model variant and (b) cache-warm procedures are followed prior to known large bursts. Failure to meet the SLO for more than 3 consecutive business hours will trigger credits calculated as a percentage of the monthly committed fee (we'll draft exact credit bands for legal).

If that pricing ladder looks reasonable, Marissa will confirm commercial approval and we can move to a term sheet with specific legal language around credits, maintenance windows, and data handling. Vivek is copied for final ops acceptance on the runbook and quantization/variant constraints.

Proposed next step: Marissa to confirm approved discount band and legal touchpoints; Tara to confirm preferred commit term (6/12/24 months) and desired burst option. After that we circulate a short-term sheet + SOC2/pen test evidence pack.

- Olga
